decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Mega Blastoise in back. Lead Sneasler + Whimsicott to threaten Talonflame/Mamoswine with Fake Out and Tailwind or outspeed under Tailwind. Backline Blastoise (Mega) + Rotom provides powerful Water/Electric offensive coverage and speed control.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has Talonflame (Focus Sash, Tailwind, Taunt, Brave Bird), Milotic (Leftovers, Competitive, Muddy Water, Icy Wind, Recover, Protect), Mamoswine (Life Orb, High Horsepower, Icicle Crash, Ice Shard, Protect), Floette-Mega (Floettite, Moonblast, Energy Ball, Protect, Helping Hand), Scrafty, and Musharna.

decisions.rationale: Intend Mega Floette. Talonflame and Scrafty lead to remove Whimsicott’s disruption and blunt Sneasler immediately: Brave Bird plus Fake Out, adapting targets if the lead differs. Mamoswine supplies the Ground-based pressure against Rotom and completes the offensive endgame, while Mega Floette threatens Blastoise and Fairy-weak targets.
decisions.notebook: Opponent reliably combines Prankster Whimsicott disruption with Scarf Rotom pressure and may repeatedly target Milotic with Thunderbolt; Rotom can remain Choice-locked into Thunderbolt. Sneasler’s Focus Sash makes early damage control important. Mega Blastoise supplies strong special spread pressure with Hydro Pump and carries Ice Beam/Aura Sphere. Prefer offensive Mega Floette plus Talonflame/Scrafty disruption control, with Mamoswine as the Ground-based pressure; do not default to Mega Floette plus Milotic.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott sets up Tailwind with Prankster priority, while Sneasler hits Scrafty with Dire Claw (ignoring Intimidate's physical drop or threatening a poison status) to chunk or cripple Scrafty before Talonflame and Scrafty can pivot out or control speed.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has Talonflame (Focus Sash, Tailwind, Taunt, Brave Bird), Milotic (Leftovers, Competitive, Muddy Water, Icy Wind, Recover, Protect), Mamoswine (Life Orb, High Horsepower, Icicle Crash, Ice Shard, Protect), Floette-Mega (Floettite, Moonblast, Energy Ball, Protect, Helping Hand), Scrafty (Sitrus Berry, Intimidate, Fake Out, Knock Off, Snarl, Drain Punch), and Musharna.

decisions.rationale: Protect blocks Sneasler’s faster Fake Out while Scrafty’s Fake Out denies Whimsicott’s Tailwind or Encore. This preserves Talonflame to KO Sneasler next turn and avoids giving Whimsicott a free disruption turn. Brave Bird immediately fails if Sneasler Fake Outs first.
decisions.notebook: Opponent reliably pairs Prankster Whimsicott disruption with Scarf Rotom pressure and may repeatedly target Milotic with Thunderbolt. Rotom can remain Choice-locked into Thunderbolt. Prefer offensive Mega Floette with Talonflame/Scrafty disruption control, using Mamoswine for Ground pressure. Mega Blastoise provides strong special spread pressure and carries Ice Beam/Aura Sphere. Sneasler’s Focus Sash makes early damage control important.

decisions.rationale: Scrafty took Fake Out last turn and is weak to Fighting; Sneasler can KO or heavily damage Scrafty with Close Combat while Whimsicott sets Tailwind. Even with Intimidate drop, Sneasler's Fighting STAB is super-effective on Scrafty.

Sneasler is at -1 Def/SpD and vulnerable to Brave Bird from Gale Wings Talonflame (+3 Unburden speed puts us ahead, but Sash is broken and HP is 63%). Bringing in Blastoise and protecting Sneasler or positioning safely lets us Mega Evolve Blastoise next turn and pressure Talonflame/Scrafty.

Brave Bird immediately guarantees the KO on Whimsicott if it acts, while Knock Off guarantees the KO on Sneasler. Sneasler may Fake Out Talonflame, but Scrafty still removes it; eliminating both active threats is stronger than setting Tailwind or relying on Taunt through Fake Out.
decisions.notebook: Opponent reliably pairs Prankster Whimsicott disruption with Scarf Rotom pressure and may repeatedly target Milotic with Thunderbolt. Rotom can remain Choice-locked into Thunderbolt. Prefer offensive Mega Floette with Talonflame/Scrafty disruption control, using Mamoswine for Ground pressure. Sneasler’s Focus Sash makes early damage control important.

decisions.rationale: Sneasler outspeeds Talonflame with Unburden and can KO Scrafty with Close Combat. Meanwhile, Blastoise Mega Evolves and threatens an OHKO on Talonflame with Hydro Pump (super-effective), securing a decisive double-target advantage in Game 3.

Protect blocks Sneasler’s priority Fake Out and Blastoise’s likely Hydro Pump while preserving Talonflame to guarantee Brave Bird into Sneasler next turn. Switching Scrafty avoids another super-effective Close Combat and brings in the intended Mega Floette at full health. This retains both offensive threats and prevents losing the board immediately.
decisions.notebook: Opponent reliably uses disruption alongside strong immediate pressure; after Whimsicott is removed, expect Sneasler priority or Protect mind games and Blastoise Water pressure. Preserve Mega Floette for the midgame and use Talonflame’s guaranteed Brave Bird to remove weakened Sneasler.

decisions.rationale: Sneasler outspeeds everything with Unburden and can fish for a poison/sleep/paralysis with Dire Claw on Floette-Eternal (2x super effective). Blastoise-Mega fires Hydro Pump into Talonflame to break its Focus Sash or KO it if it doesn't protect, bypassing Talonflame's Protect/Brave Bird mindgame.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Brave Bird guarantees the KO on Sneasler unless it Protects. Mega Energy Ball punishes that Protect line with super-effective pressure on Blastoise, while still contributing if Sneasler attacks or uses Fake Out. Double-targeting Sneasler gives Blastoise too much freedom to Protect and preserve its Water pressure.
decisions.notebook: Opponent reliably pairs disruption or Protect mind games with immediate pressure. After Whimsicott is removed, Sneasler remains the priority/Protect pivot while Mega Blastoise supplies strong Water pressure. Preserve Mega Floette for the midgame when possible; Talonflame’s Brave Bird is a guaranteed KO on weakened Sneasler.

decisions.rationale: Mamoswine is the only switch that immediately threatens a guaranteed KO on Blastoise at 12% with High Horsepower. Scrafty provides no immediate listed pressure and leaves the weakened Floette exposed. Passing with Floette avoids risking its final HP while Mamoswine forces the key Protect-or-lose decision.
decisions.notebook: Opponent reliably combines disruption or Protect mind games with immediate offensive pressure. After removing Whimsicott, Sneasler functioned as the priority/Protect pivot while Mega Blastoise supplied Water pressure. Preserve Mega Floette when possible; weakened Sneasler was vulnerable to Talonflame Brave Bird.

decisions.rationale: Rotom outspeeds Mamoswine (235 vs 132 max) and can KO 10% Floette-Mega with Shadow Ball. Blastoise-Mega is at 13% and threatened by Mamoswine's Ice Shard (priority +1) or Floette Helping Hand, so Protect or Hydro Pump into Mamoswine secures the field.
decisions.notebook: Rotom Choice Scarf outspeeds Mamoswine and paralyzed Floette-Mega. Blastoise-Mega has low HP.

decisions.rationale: High Horsepower removes the faster Rotom before it can act, while Energy Ball should remove Blastoise at 12% and is the strongest reliable listed attack into it. If Rotom targets Floette, both foes are still eliminated before their attacks matter; if either Protects, the surviving endgame remains favorable.
decisions.notebook: Opponent reliably combines Protect or disruption with immediate offensive pressure, especially around Mega Blastoise. Preserve Mega Floette when practical, but prioritize removing faster threats and deny free super-effective Water pressure on Mamoswine.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.
Rotom outspeeds and hits Mamoswine with Shadow Ball while Blastoise-Mega uses Aura Sphere for super-effective damage on Mamoswine and Scrafty.
decisions.notebook: Rotom is Choice Scarfed and outspeeds the remaining opposing field. Blastoise-Mega can break remaining targets with Aura Sphere and Hydro Pump.

decisions.rationale: Mamoswine’s High Horsepower guarantees the KO on Blastoise from 12%, while Scrafty’s Knock Off guarantees the OHKO on Rotom. Rotom moves first but is locked into resisted Shadow Ball and cannot stop either KO; this removes both threats even if Blastoise Protects.
decisions.notebook: Opponent reliably combines Protect or disruption with immediate offensive pressure, especially around Mega Blastoise. Prioritize removing faster threats and deny free super-effective Water pressure on Mamoswine.

decisions.rationale: Rotom has fainted, so its slot must pass. Blastoise-Mega uses Aura Sphere against Scrafty, which is super-effective and securely KOs the remaining 48% HP Scrafty to win Game 3 and the series.

Mamoswine is fainted, so pass is forced. Drain Punch targets the only live threat and is a guaranteed KO from 12%, while restoring Scrafty if it connects. Knock Off also KOs, but provides no recovery. Protect is the main opposing denial line.
decisions.notebook: Opponent reliably pairs Mega Blastoise offensive pressure with Protect or disruption. Prioritize removing faster threats and deny free super-effective Water pressure on Mamoswine.

reflections.summary: Mega Blastoise and late-game positioning broke through the opponent's Mamoswine and Scrafty after Sneasler and Rotom eliminated priority and speed threats.
reflections.adjustment: Retain the core composition and fast offensive pacing, ensuring proper defensive positioning against priority Brave Bird and Ice Shard.
reflections.notebook: Opponent's core features Talonflame, Mamoswine, Scrafty, and Mega Floette. Mamoswine runs Life Orb with High Horsepower and Ice Shard; Scrafty runs Sitrus Berry and Intimidate; Floette carries Fairy Aura and Energy Ball.

reflections.summary: The loss was primarily a team-preview mismatch: Mega Floette and Mamoswine offered poor answers to Mega Blastoise's repeated super-effective pressure, while the four brought were vulnerable to the opponent's fast disruption and coverage. The game was effectively decided by the matchup plan rather than execution errors.
reflections.adjustment: Do not center the next game on Mega Floette plus Mamoswine into Mega Blastoise. Bring Hippowdon and Clefable instead, using their defensive utility and Protect to deny Blastoise free attacks while preserving Talonflame for speed control.
reflections.notebook: Mega Blastoise consistently uses Protect and strong Hydro Pump/Aura Sphere pressure to punish exposed targets. The opponent also supports it with fast disruption and offensive coverage from Sneasler, Whimsicott, and Rotom. Against this structure, avoid relying on Mega Floette/Mamoswine as the core; prioritize Hippowdon/Clefable-style defensive counterplay and preserve Talonflame for speed control.
